newsitem.title: USA: Chevron Q3 upstream boosted by crude prices.
newsitem.headline: Chevron Q3 upstream boosted by crude prices.

text.p: Chevron Corp said Monday third quarter profits from its exploration and production business were boosted by higher crude and natural gas prices while those higher prices hurt its refining and marketing business.
"We had another strong quarter," said Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Ken Derr.
"Our worldwide upstream operations turned in excellent results on higher crude oil and natural gas prices and continued increases in our international production volumes," he added.
While exploration and production segment results were boosted by the higher prices, the downstream business saw lower refining margins on the higher prices.
"On the downstream side, the higher crude oil prices, coupled with softening product prices, have squeezed product margins, both domestically and internationally," Derr said.
Downstream third quarter operating earnings were lower than the previous quarter and the comparable year-ago period.
Derr said that on balance the firm was having an "excellent" year adding that programs aimed at improving profitability are working while industry conditions have improved.

Chevron said annualized return on employed capital, excluding special items, has risen to 12.5 percent this year from 9.8 percent for 1995. The company said it has reduced its debt by over $850 million this year.
Earlier Chevron posted third quarter profits of $655 million or $1.00 a share compared to $282 million or $0.44 a share in the year-ago period.
The results for the latest quarter were boosted by a net $5 million from special items, the 1995 quarter included special charges of $222 million.
Excluding special items in both periods, 1996 third quarter results of $650 million increased 29 percent from $504 million in last year's third quarter.
Revenues for the quarter were $11.0 billion, up 18 percent from $9.3 billion in the year-ago period.
